Commentary.Commentary: We are back for Zimbabwe's second innings! The umpires are back out in the middle as the West Indian players are seen in a huddle right around the boundary ropes. Innocent Kaia and Tanunurwa Makoni are the openers for Zimbabwe. Alzarri Joseph has the brand-new cherry in hand and is ready to steam in. Let's play...
... 3rd Innings ...

Right then, Zimbabwe will be happy with the fact that they only conceded 2 runs before restricting West Indies to 292 runs but the visitors still have a big first-innings lead of 177 runs. The overhead conditions should help the Windies pacers and the hosts will have to be at their best with the bat in order to keep themselves in the game. A fascinating phase of play awaits and join us in a few minutes to catch Zimbabwe's second innings.

Well, that was quick! Less than a couple of overs bowled in the day and West Indies have lost both their remaining wickets and are bundled out for 292. Jason Holder who walked out alongside Gudakesh Motie faced the first ball of the day but was edged out while going after a wide one and soon enough, Motie was caught in the deep. Victor Nyauchi who finished Day 2 with 3 wickets in the kitty, went out to pick up his first five-wicket haul in Test cricket.

OUT! CAUGHT! Victor Nyauchi gets a fi-fer here. This is a short ball, on leg stump. Motie goes back, swivels and pulls it in front of square on the leg side. Brandon Mavuta runs to his right in the deep and takes a good catch diving forward. West Indies have been bowled out for 292 runs.
Commentary.Howout: c Brandon Mavuta b Victor Nyauchi

Commentary.Commentary: Touch fuller, on leg stump. Motie dances down the track and drills it to long on. Although denies the single here, as he thinks he can score a boundary himself.
A slower length ball, around off. Motie taps it to point.
Length and outside off. Shannon Gabriel looks to chase it but misses. So, West Indies have added just two runs so far.
A length ball, drifting down leg. Gabriel does not bother.
A single now as this is smacked down to deep point.
A well-directed bouncer, in the channel. Motie tries to heave it away but misses.

NO BALL! Zimbabwe were ready to walk off the field but Tanaka Chivanga has faltered on this occassion and has his wicket ruled out. It is a short ball, wide outside off. Motie gets an under-edge on it. Tafadzwa Tsiga gathers it safely but it is ruled out as Chivanga's back foot lands on the tramline and hence, Gudakesh Motie survives.
Tanaka Chivanga once again bends his back hard and serves it around middle. Gudakesh Motie is unable to put it away.
A well-directed bouncer, outside off. Motie makes room and looks to hammer it over backward point but misses.
Tanaka Chivanga (13-0-57-0) to bowl from the other end.
A length ball, tailing in from outside off. Shannon Gabriel takes a blow high on his pads.
Shannon Gabriel is the last man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Jason Holder slips out on the very first delivery on the moving day. It is a length ball, wide of off. Jason Holder slashes hard at it but only manages to get a thick outside edge. Tafadzwa Tsiga makes no mistakes behind the sticks. The wicket could've been ruled out but Victor Nyauchi has some part of his foot behind the line.
Commentary.Howout: c Tafadzwa Tsiga b Victor Nyauchi

Commentary.Commentary: Finally, we are all set for play to begin on Day 3! The umpires are out in the middle and so are the players of Zimbabwe. The overnight batters for West Indies, Jason Holder and Gudakesh Motie also make their way out to the middle. It will be Victor Nyauchi to start proceedings with the ball and will complete his unfinished over from the previous day. Also, Lunch will be taken at 4.30 pm IST (11 am GMT). Let's play...

Update 2.36 pm IST (9.06 am GMT) - There is some good news as broadcasters are said to come 'On Air' at 2.58 pm IST (9.28 am GMT) which means play could start at 3 pm IST (9.30 am GMT). The Zimbabwe bowlers are also seen warming up and this means that in all likelihood play will start at the above-mentioned time. It is confirmed now and there will be 75 overs bowled in the day, light and weather permitting that is. So, buckle up as we aren't that far away from the start of play on Day 3.

Update 2.09 pm IST (8.39 am GMT) - The umpires were out in the middle a few minutes ago. There is no rain but there are clouds all over the ground. The outfield seems to have improved a bit and there will be another inspection at 2.30 pm IST (9 am GMT). Hopefully, the next inspection comes bearing good news. Stick around for more updates.

Update 1.19 pm IST (7.49 am GMT) - The umpires have scheduled an inspection for 2 pm IST (8.30 am GMT). We should, hopefully, have a clear idea of the outfield and if conditions improve or not by then. Stay tuned for more updates.

Update 1.05 pm IST (7.35 am GMT) - Darlington Matambanadzo is near the deck. He informs that there is a rough patch at the fuller length, which the spinners would hope to capitalize on. He adds that the batting conditions will only get tougher from hereon. Adds that if West Indies get the lead to 220, then Zimbabwe will certainly find it a difficult chase. He then inspects the outfield as well and says that there are a few areas of concern and the umpires are out too to just have a look. Stick around for further updates as the early start has now been delayed.

Update 12.48 pm IST (7.18 am GMT) - The live scenes from the ground currently depict that there isn't any rain around but the outfield seems to be wet and there's standing water on one area of the ground. The groundsmen are working hard to get it ready in time for the play to start and the Super Sopper is at work as well. Stay tuned for further updates.

West Indies have a sizeable lead and still have a couple of wickets in hand thanks to a spirited fightback by Joshua Da Silva and Roston Chase on Day 2. They will look to extend this lead to beyond the 200-run mark and hope that their bowlers work their magic just like the first innings and they don't have to bat one more time. Well, that is a scenario for later but for now, the main focus for them would be trying to stay at the crease for as long as possible. A crucial first session in which one team can simply take the game away or the other team can crawl their way back into the match. Which side will make early inroads on Day 3? Stay tuned to find out.

After being bowled out early on Day 1, the hosts, Zimbabwe did make a few amends with the ball on that day itself and it looked like they wouldn't concede a big first-innings lead. That being said, on a rain-hit Day 2, their bowlers were able to repeat the performance from the previous evening. They are trailing by 175 runs and will need to bundle out the opposition quickly in order to have a small chance of getting a favourable result. Victor Nyauchi will certainly be the key for them.

Hello and welcome to Day 3 of the 2nd and final Test match between Zimbabwe and West Indies at the Queens Sports Club in Bulawayo. Day 3 is known as the moving day in Test cricket and given where the game is currently, this day could prove to be decisive, that is if the rain gods stay away. The good news is that the forecast for most of the day is good and we should, hopefully, get plenty of cricketing action.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The day belonged to three individuals. Roston Chase and Joshua Da Silva played decent knocks and their partnership helped West Indies to swell the lead. The Zimbabwean bowling was disciplined but they didn't create enough wicket-taking opportunities in the first half. There was a small window of play when the action resumed after Tea and Victor Nyauchi's double strike handed the hosts some semblance of hope. They are behind by a big margin in this Test and all will eventually depend on how they bat the second time around. Hopefully, we will get all the answers on Day 3. As expected, there will be an early start, at 1 pm IST (7.30 am GMT), do join us in advance for the build-up. Cheers!

It's indeed Stumps on Day 2. Less than 50 overs were possible but still, this Test match has moved ahead decently, all thanks to those 14 wickets that fell on Day 1. West Indies now lead by 175 runs and still have two wickets remaining. The weather is going to be a concern in the coming days as well, so the visitors will have to take a call. We could get the declaration as a lead of 175 is looking good enough for this surface. Anyway, we will wait and watch what happens.
Update 8.43 pm IST (3.13 pm GMT) - If we heard the announcement on the ground correctly, it's Stumps on Day 2. We will get you the confirmation soon.

Update 8.15 pm IST (2.45 pm GMT) - IT'S RAINING! The groundsmen are given the green signal and they run out to cover the pitch and the surroundings. This is very frustrating for the players. They are off again. A little period of play was only possible and Zimbabwe enjoyed it the most by picking up the wickets of Joshua Da Silva and Alzarri Joseph. The lead has stretched to 175 runs. The rain is picking up its intensity now. It looks unlikely to have more overs on Day 2 as the light will also start to deteriorate now. Let's see what's in store.
Angling in again, on a length around off, Holder wrists it across the line but finds mid-wicket.
Angling away outside off, on a good length, Motie stays back and taps it down to backward point for a single.
Dark clouds are building again. The sun is out at the moment but the groundsmen are not taking any chance this time and are ready with the covers.
Fuller and around off, Holder drives it towards extra cover for one.
Outside off, Holder tries to cut but misses.
Length delivery drifting down the leg side, Motie looks to flick but misses out as the keeper collects.
Good-length delivery on top of the off stump, Motie drives this but couldn't find the gap at covers.
Short one angling down the leg side by Chivanga, Motie just manages to sway away from it.
Fuller length around off, Motie pushes it towards cover.
EDGY FOUR! Flashes and flashes hard. Full in length and wide outside off, Motie throws his bat at it and edges it wide of the gully fielder for a boundary. Lead moves to 173.
Good-length delivery angling into the pads, Holder tries to flick but misses. It deflects this off the pads towards the square-leg region for a single. Leg-bye signalled.
Overpitched delivery outside the off-stump line, Motie has lofted this over the fielder at mid off for a couple.
Good-length delivery just outside off, Holder tries to push at it but gets an inside edge. It dribbles away to square leg and they cross.
Full and wide outside the off stump, Holder leaves this for the keeper to collect.
Length delivery drifting down the leg side, Holder misses out on a push as the ball hits his pads. Loud appeal but the umpire turned it down. Going down!
Length delivery angled into the right-hander, Holder pokes at this but gets beaten by the bounce as it keeps a tad low.
Innocent Kaia has hurt himself and is in immense pain. The physio has rushed out. It was a regulation stop but it seems that Kaia is hit near the groin area.
Ouch! Fuller delivery outside the off-stump line, Holder drives it towards the cover region where Innocent Kaia goes down low to stop the ball but misses and is hit in a very uncomfortable spot.
A dot to end the over. Short-pitched delivery towards the ribs, Motie ducks down this one.
Fuller delivery outside the off-stump line, Motie leaves this one.
Length delivery going away outside off, Motie lets it go.
Chivanga oversteps as he tries to put extra effort into this delivery. Length delivery around off, Motie has blocked it on the leg side but this will be bowled again by Chivanga.
Good-length delivery angling away from the bat of Motie, He pokes at this and misses out.
Good-length delivery in the middle, Holder gets a thick inside edge and the deflection off his pads takes it toward the square leg region. Single taken.
Around off, the batter has just watchfully blocked this out.
Fuller and on off, pushed to mid on. End of a successful over for Victor Nyauchi.
Outside off, pushed with an angled bat to cover-point.
FOUR! West Indies are in a hurry now. Short in length and around middle, Gudakesh Motie rides the bounce and pulls it in front of square on the leg side for a boundary.
Gudakesh Motie is the new batter.

OUT! CAUGHT! Nyauchi has taken his second wicket in the over as he gets rid of Alzarri Joseph with a lethal short delivery. The pacer bends his back and delivers it around off, Alzarri Joseph tries to be aggressive and attempts to pull. But there's some extra bounce and Joseph fails to control his shot. The ball flies off the top edge and Tanunurwa Makoni moves back from mid-wicket to take a fantastic catch. Zimbabwe have certainly benefitted from the rain-break.
Commentary.Howout: c Tanunurwa Makoni b Victor Nyauchi

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Fine timing! Angling down the leg side, Alzarri Joseph picks it off his pads and clips it behind square leg for a boundary.
Alzarri Joseph walks in next. He loves to use the long handle. Let's see his approach.

OUT! Sound of timber! Victor Nyauchi strikes again and it's a perfect start for the home team after the break. Slightly short in length, around off and shaping in sharply. Joshua Da Silva hangs on the back foot, trying to defend but plays down the wrong line. He correctly expected it to shape in but it moves back in lesser than his anticipation. The ball beats the bat and meets the stumps. West Indies lead by 155 runs!
Revised playing conditions for the day - 29 overs to be bowled, light permitting. The play can go on till 10 pm IST (4.30 pm GMT).
Good-length delivery angling in towards the batter, Holder gets beaten by the pace of it as the ball hits his pads. This was going a bit above the stumps.
Fuller delivery outside off, Da Silva gets tempted and drives this towards the left of a diving mid-off fielder as they take a single.
Good-length delivery around off, Da Silva has pushed this towards cover for another dot.
Lands it on a good length, around middle, Da Silva defends it off the back foot.

Appeal for a caught behind! Back of a length, around leg and angling down, Joshua Da Silva tries to glance but fails to connect. There is some noise as it goes to the keeper and they appeal. Nothing from the umpire. Maybe, it came off the thigh pad.
The players are back on the ground and the wait is over. Tanaka Chivanga to continue with his over.
... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

Update 7.31 pm IST (2.01 pm GMT) - It appears that we're minutes away from resumption. The stumps are back in place. Bright sunshine. We'll get a clearer picture in another 10 minutes. A few players are going through the warm-up drills.

Update 7.11 pm IST (1.41 pm GMT) - The groundsmen are putting in the hard yards. The big covers are off and now only the pitch is having the protection sheet. There are a few wet patches on the ground and that is the only area of concern. Super Sopers continue to do the rounds. And as I type, the pitch is also uncovered. There could be an official inspection soon. Stay tuned.

Update 6.48 pm IST (1.18 pm GMT) - Good news, folks! The rain has eased off and we can see some blue skies as well. The groundsmen are carefully peeling off the covers to dry. One Super Sopper is also doing the rounds. Things are certainly looking promising as the sun has also marked its presence. This will surely aid the ground staff in drying out the outfield. Stay tuned, we might get some more good news soon.

Update 5.52 pm IST (12.22 pm GMT) - With the conditions not improving much, the umpires have decided to take TEA ON DAY 2. West Indies started the afternoon session with consecutive boundaries and it appeared that they will press on the accelerator but Zimbabwe smartly bowled disciplined lines and soon dried out the runs. The second new ball resulted in a breakthrough for them as Victor Nyauchi breached the defense of Roston Chase with a beautiful delivery. The visitors managed 33 runs off 14.1 overs in the second session before the rain gods intervened. As I'm typing, the rain has started to come down heavily. It is looking very dull and the chances are very less for a resumption soon. Stay with us for latest updates.
Update 5.32 pm IST (12.02 pm GMT) - No fresh news from the ground. The covers are on and although the intensity of the rain has reduced, it is still persistent. Stay tuned, we will keep you posted.

Update 5.12 pm IST (11.42 am GMT) - It's raining properly now. The dark clouds started to pull in but no one expected the rain to arrive so soon. The groundsmen are caught a bit unaware and are seen rushing to pick the covers. The players have already exited. It's pelting down now. More and more covers are coming on. It seems like a lengthy delay. Let's stay positive.
Fuller-length delivery drifting down the leg side, Da Silva has flicked this towards short mid-wicket.
Tanaka Chivanga comes into the attack. 10-0-50-0 are the figures of the debutant so far. The wind has picked up and it has gone quite dark. In fact, it has started to drizzle.
Fuller and closer to off, Holder is on the front foot in defense. A wicket maiden for Victor Nyauchi!

Drinks break. A crucial breakthrough for the hosts but they need to keep chipping away at the wickets as the West Indian lead is already 150-plus. The second new ball is their best bet and they will hope that the wicket of Roston Chase will open up one end for them. Jason Holder is the new batter.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Victor Nyauchi dishes out a peach of a delivery and goes through the defense of the batter. He puts it on a fuller length around off and gets it to nip into the batter off the seam. Roston Chase tries to drive down the ground but misses as the ball sneaks through the tiny gap between bat and pad to find the stumps. End of a good knock from Chase. West Indies lead by 154 runs.
Around middle, on a good length, Chase covers the line well and defends it on the leg side.
Drifting down the leg side, on a length, Chase tries to flick but misses. It's a good diving take by the keeper, Tafadzwa Tsiga.
Slightly short and on off, Chase hangs back inside the crease and cuts it to point.
Full in length and around off, Chase chooses to stay back in defense.
Tossed up outside off, turning away, Joshua Da Silva allows it through.
Arm ball around off, Joshua defends it by getting half forward.
Short and on off, punched through covers for a brace.
Fuller and on off, Da Silva strokes down to mid off.
The batter has just watchfully blocked this out.
Flatter and shorter on off, Chase gets back inside the crease and forces it to long off for a single.
Fuller and around off, Chase strokes it off the front foot to point where Makoni once again makes an excellent partial stop. One more run to end the over. Lead is now above 150!
Gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it well.
Angling down the leg side, Joshua Da Silva works it to deep square leg for a single.
Pitches it up and around off, Joshua again drives it down the ground but finds mid off.
Too full and on off, driven off the front foot to mid off.
Fuller in length and outside off, Da Silva leans into the drive and forces it towards point. Tanunurwa Makoni dives across to his right and saves a certain boundary. Only one run is taken.
Flighted around middle, defended back to the bowler.
Tossed up around off, Chase pushes it gently to cover-point and picks up a run.
Quicker arm ball around off, Chase has his bat down in time as he blocks.
Floated and around off, it's pushed off the front foot to covers.
Gets forward to a full ball and drives it through covers for a couple.
Flatter and shorter, on off, Chase goes on the back foot and plays it down to covers.
Wellington Masakadza (18-5-52-1) to share the second new ball from the opposite end.
Shortish and on off, Chase gets back and plays it down to cover-point for a single.
Beaten all ends up! Victor serves it full and outside off, nipping away a hint, Chase chases a wide delivery, and attempts to drive but gets beaten.
On a length and outside off, angling in, Chase takes a step forward to cover the stumps and allows it through.
Fullish and on middle, Roston shows the full face of the bat and caresses it down the ground. The fielder from mid on cuts it off and they get a couple.
Pitches it up and around off, Chase drives but straight to short cover.
Back of a length, outside off at a gentle pace, Chase shows respect and lets it be.
The second new ball is available now and Zimbabwe have taken it. Victor Nyauchi is back on.
Flatter trajectory this time, Da Silva pulls it hard but the fielder at mid-wicket fields well.

FOUR! Good shot! Brandon Mavuta drags it short on middle, not for the first time in this session and Joshua Da Silva rocks back to pull it to deep mid-wicket, also not for the first time in this session. Lead is 142 now.
Mavuta pulls the length back a bit, Da Silva has blocked this out.
Fuller-length delivery around off, Da Silva drives it back towards the bowler.

Overpitched delivery in the middle, Da SIlva drills this straight into the arms of the fielder at mid on.
Fuller-length delivery towards the middle, Da Silva has pushed this toward the cover fielder.
Good-length delivery just outside the line of off, Da Silva has guided this towards point.
Short and wide outside the off-stump line, Da Silva has cut this to the fielder at point.
Fuller-length delivery around the off, Da Silva gets an inside edge towards the mid on.
Wide for height as Tiripano darts one in way too short.
Good-length delivery towards the top of off stump, Da Silva has punched this towards the fielder at cover.
Good-length delivery outside the off-stump line, Da Silva has punched this towards wide long off for a single.
Fuller length outside the off, Chase pushes at it and edges it past first slip for a single.
On middle, defended to the leg side.
Forces a short delivery to extra cover. The fielder parries it behind to mid off and they cross.
Flighted and on off, defended.
Tossed-up delivery just outside the line of off, Da Silva has drilled this back to the bowler.
Serves it on a good length, outside the off stump, Chase has pushed this towards the off side to end this over.
Good length just outside the line of stumps, Chase has blocked this out solidly off the front foot.
On a good length outside the off-stump line, Da Silva has punched this towards extra cover for a single.
Around off, that is defended solidly off the front foot.
Length delivery angling into the pads, Chase flicks towards square leg for a single.
Good-length delivery on the pads, Chase works it away towards the mid-wicket region.
Length delivery around off, Silva defends it back towards the bowler.
Back of a length outside off, Silva lets it go into the bucket gloves of the keeper.
Leans forward and pushes a full ball back to the bowler.
Tossed up outside the off-stump line, Da Silva has pushed this towards the off side for no run.
Fuller delivery into the line of stumps, Da Silva leans ahead and gets an inside edge to it, onto his pads.

Drifting down the leg side, Chase attempts to flick but misses.

Around middle, on a length, Chase works it with the angle of the bowler but finds mid-wicket.
Angles in a length ball around off, Chase covers the line and blocks it down safely.
Lunges to a full ball and defends it with his bat and pad together.
Short and outside off, Da Silva cuts it with the spin to point.
Flights this up, around middle, Joshua goes nice and deep before playing it back to the bowler.
Drags his length short, around off, Chase rocks back and punches it to sweeper cover for a single.
Loopy and full, around middle, Chase pushes it back to the bowler.
Flighted and around leg, Chase defends it near his front pad.
Slower one, full and around off, Da Silva drives it down the ground but straight to mid off.
Serves it full and on middle, Joshua Da Silva flicks but finds short mid-wicket.
Lands it on a good length, around off, Joshua stands back and punches it to mid on.
Angling down the leg side, Chase flicks it to the left of mid-wicket and pinches a quick run.
Full and outside off, Chase drives on the off side but doesn't find the gap.
Uses the angle of the bowler and works a length ball to mid-wicket.
Donald Tiripano to bowl from the other end.
Floated and full, on middle, pushed down to mid on.
On middle, helped to mid-wicket.
Again the length is dragged down, on middle, Joshua punches it with a heavy bottom hand but finds mid-wicket.
A touch slower this time, around leg and turning towards middle, Joshua stands deep inside the crease and defends it on the leg side.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries to start the afternoon session. Quicker one, short and around leg, Joshua goes back and tickles it fine down to fine leg for a boundary.
FOUR! A good way to start the session! Mavuta serves it short and on middle, Da Silva picks the length in a jiffy, goes on the back foot and powers it past mid-wicket for a boundary.

We're back. The players have made their way out to the middle. Zimbabwe are in desperate need of a fruitful session to stay in the hunt. Can they pick up a few quick wickets? Let's find out. Brandon Mavuta to start proceedings. Here we go...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

West Indies are now in a great position and their aim will be to bat Zimbabwe out of the game. This pitch has certainly some support for the bowlers and it's only going to deteriorate more. Let's see if the hosts could bounce back and have some say in the post-Lunch session which will begin at 4.10 pm IST (10.40 am GMT).

The morning session belonged to West Indies. They scored 103 runs for the loss of Kyle Mayers's wicket and have extended their lead to 121 runs. Roston Chase has batted with full control and his current partnership with Joshua Da Silva has pushed the home team firmly on the back foot. Despite bowling disciplined lines, Zimbabwe failed to create many wicket-taking opportunities and are staring down the barrel. They needed wickets in a heap to make a comeback but that didn't happen.
Flighted delivery, landing full around off, Chase lunges and offers an angled bat. It rolls to point. That will be Lunch on Day 2.
Short and wide outside off, Da Silva cuts it through point for a single.
Loopy and around middle, Joshua flicks it towards mid on.
Leans forward to a full ball and pushes it back to the bowler.
Short and outside off, played down to point for one.
Skidding down the leg side, Chase fails to sweep and it goes off his pads to fine leg. They take two leg byes.
Final over before Lunch.
Dropped? Loopy and full, around off, Joshua drives it firmly and it goes quickly to the silly point fielder. It hits his right arm and goes down. A tough change but an opportunity nonetheless.
Tossed up outside off, left alone.
Fuller and on middle, perhaps the arm ball, Da Silva pushes it from the inner half to mid on.
FOUR! Well done! Wellington digs it in short, around middle and leg, Joshua Da Silva rocks back and pulls it with authority to the deep square leg fence.
Floated and full, around off, Chase drives it past the fielder at extra cover and takes a single.
Delivers it short and on off, Chase easily goes on the back foot and punches it to sweeper cover for a run.
Hangs this up in the air and gets it to drift in around off, Da Silva drives it to long off and keeps strike with a run.
Short and wide outside off, Chase gets back and cuts it to deep cover for a run.
Gets on the front foot and defends it with gentle hands.
Extra flight this time, full and on off, Joshua strokes it down through mid off for a single.

Edgy! Flighted and outside off, a bit on the shorter side as it spins away, Chase pushes inside the line and edges it wide of first slip. Chamu Chibhabha does well to pull it back near the fence at third man and saves one run for his team.
Bowls it short and outside off, Joshua goes back and eases it through covers for a single.
Quicker arm ball on middle, Chase goes on the back foot and keeps it out safely to covers.
Fullish and landing around off, Chase pushes it to short cover.
Flighted and full around off, Chase wrists it down to mid on.
Goes short and on off, Joshua Da Silva is on the back foot as he forces it to sweeper cover for a single.
Appeal for an lbw! Not given. Tossed up around off, turning away a shade, Joshua leans forward to defend but misses. He is rapped on the pads but the impact is outside the line of the stumps.
FIFTY FOR CHASE! Loopy delivery, full and around off, Chase pushes it gently to point for a run. A well-controlled knock from Roston as he brings up his 11th Test fifty.
Fuller and on off, Joshua Da Silva strides forward and drives it to covers.
Flatter arm ball on middle, Joshua defends it ahead of his front pad.
Serves it short and on off, Joshua goes back and punches it to short extra cover.
Fuller and on off, driven to deep cover for a single.
Bowls it wide of the crease and fires in a full ball on middle, Chase chooses to play it from the back foot and keeps it out towards mid-wicket.
Begins his spell with a short ball on middle, Chase goes on the back foot and hits it wide of mid on for a couple. Lead is now 100 runs!
Spin from both ends now. Milton Shumba comes into the attack. He has bowled only one over so far.
Slower through the air, full and on middle, Joshua presses forward in defense.
The length is fuller this time and it's easily driven to sweeper cover for a run.
Flatter and shorter on middle, Chase punches off the back foot on the leg side where the mid-wicket fielder makes a diving stop.
Brilliant delivery. A bit of turn and bounce from around off, Chase pushes at it from the crease and misses.
Wellington Masakadza goes short and wide outside off, Joshua Da Silva hangs back and cracks it to sweeper cover for a single.
Flighted and on off, Chase eases it down to long off for a single.
Slower delivery to end the over from Tiripano. Da Silva reads it well and has blocked this out.
Length delivery in the middle, Chase opens up the face of his bat as he guides this towards backward point for a single.
Fuller delivery in the middle, Chase has driven this crisply but straight towards the fielder at short extra cover.
Length delivery outside the off-stump line, Chase has driven this towards the fielder at extra cover for no run. This kept a tad low.
Fuller delivery in the middle, Chase strides forward to block this out.
Bouncer from Tiripano, Chase looks to pull this but misses out.

Pitch report - The pitch is bone dry but at one end there is a good covering of grass whereas, at the other, it's completely bald. It's going to assist the spinners and the batting is going to get tougher, especially against the spinners.

The idea from Zimbabwe was right but not the execution. It's always better to bat first on a dry surface as it only gets difficult with time. The hosts though failed to take home the advantage of winning the toss. Gudakesh Motie utilized the conditions to perfection by claiming a 7-wicket haul and made a complete mockery of the Zimbabwean batting line-up. Getting only 115 in the first inning of a Test match will always make you play catch up and the home team is doing that exactly. Their hope of making a comeback relies on this morning's session, as picking wickets in a heap, will allow them to get back on level terms. Will that happen?

Welcome, ladies and gentlemen! The second day of the second Test match is upon us. This game has moved on at a brisk pace after 14 wickets fell on the first day. West Indies have gathered the early advantage but on this tricky surface, conducive for the spinners, you are never in as a batter. So, the plans for the tourists will be to carefully navigate through the morning session and stretch their lead as much as possible. Batting last won't be easy here and West Indies will be having that in mind too. Let's see how they approach the day's play. Stay tuned for more.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Zimbabwe would be disappointed with their batting effort at the end of the day. Yes, there was help for the spinners but it is not an unplayable pitch by any stretch of imagination and Windies batters just needed to apply themselves. They could not do so and apart from Kaia and Ervine no batter showed the application to stay in the middle. We should also credit Donald Tiripano for taking his side over the 100-run mark but the bowlers have been left to do too much here. They have managed to pick four wickets though and Brandon Mavuta and Wellington Masakadza have bowled well and for Zimbabwe, the first session of Day 2 will be very crucial of they want to make a comeback in this game. The first session of Day 2 will start at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). Our build-up though starts early. So do join us for the same. Cheers!

The day started with Craig Ervine winning the toss and deciding to bat first on a dry looking pitch. The idea was to get runs on the board before it starts turning. However, Windies bowlers were up to the task and Gudakesh Motie got some good turn in the first session itself as Zimbabwe lost half of their side in the first session with Motie taking two and Holder too bowling a good spell. In the second session, though it was all about Motie as he proved too hot to handle for the hosts and ended with a seven-wicket haul as Zimbabwe were bundled out for just 115. With the bat, they lost their skipper Kraigg Brathwaite early but Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Raymon Reifer stitched a nice partnership of 73 runs before West Indies went onto lose some quick wickets towards the end of the day. They are in a commanding position in this game now and would be looking to make this lead as big as possible on Day 2.

The West Indies are at the driver's seat at the end of Day 1! Zimbabwe though have managed to get three wickets in the final session and have just about managed to keep themselves in the game here. Overall, though they would need to do a lot of heavy lifting to get ahead of West Indies from hereon and things don't look good for them at the moment with West Indies already ahead by 18 runs and have six wickets in hand.

Right then, Zimbabwe will be looking for some quick wickets while West Indies will be hoping for both of these batters to end the day for them. Can the Zimbabwean bowlers come up with something special here? We shall find out together. Do join us at 6.30 pm IST (1 pm GMT) for the final session of Day 1.

Earlier in the session, Zimbabwe resumed from 70/5. Gudakesh Motie continued his good work from session one and made the home side suffer with his accurate bowling. He ended up picking seven wickets for his team and they managed to bundle Zimbabwe for just 115 runs. It was Donald Tiripano who scored an unbeaten 23 runs and took his team over the 100-run mark.

West Indies have lost one of their openers but they still have their noses in front as they trail by just 94 runs with 9 wickets in hand. They have managed to bundle Zimbabwe on just 115 runs. Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Raymon Reifer are in the middle now and they would like to build a solid partnership that can take this game away from Zimbabwe now. Tagenarine Chanderpaul is on 14 runs while Raymon Reifer has just arrived. Zimbabwe bowlers have got a wicket of the dangerous Kraigg Brathwaite and it was Wellington Masakadza who chipped in. They will look to pick some more and claw their way back in this game.
